model.title: Accelerating Access to Critical Therapies for ALS Reauthorization Act of 2026
model.meta: Energy and Commerce Committee · Rep. Mike Quigley (D-IL)

summary.text: The bill would extend funding through fiscal year 2031 for federal programs supporting research and development of treatments for ALS and other neurodegenerative diseases, including grants from the National Institutes of Health and Food and Drug Administration, as well as a partnership between the two agencies. It would also require the NIH to evaluate the safety and efficacy of experimental drugs and mandate that researchers report serious side effects, while directing the FDA to develop and publish a five-year plan to advance drug development and expand access to investigational treatments for these diseases.
